sm: The Napa Legal Institute released its fourth annual Faith and Freedom Index on November 16, ranking all fifty states and the District of Columbia across fifteen categories affecting churches, religious schools, pregnancy resource centers and other faith-based nonprofits. Alabama scored highest at eighty percent, followed by Kansas at seventy-six, Indiana at seventy-five and Texas at seventy-one. Michigan scored lowest at thirty-four percent, then Washington at thirty-eight and Massachusetts at forty-one. The rankings do not follow party lines; New York, for example, outscored North Dakota, South Carolina and Tennessee. Frank DeVito of Napa Legal said many of the most important rules involve governance, taxes, audit thresholds and exemptions rather than culture-war issues, and he blamed Michigan's score on burdensome nondiscrimination rules, no state religious freedom act, a Blaine amendment and no emergency protections. Since last year, Florida, Massachusetts and Rhode Island improved their standing, and DeVito urged voters to consider how state laws burden religion.
